transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-11-25
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (TerraData), Dana Ortiz (TerraData SRE), Luca Romano (TerraData Security), Emma Shaw (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on networking/peering progress, results from the 50k-token benchmark run, discussion about upgrade to runtime 1.2, and next steps for KMS/HSM confirmation and routing rules. A few minor routing issues remain; team to share peering details and Jordan will push small config changes.

Topics: Networking, Routing/NAT, Upgrade plan (runtime 1.2), Perf tuning, Security/KMS

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have like 45 minutes. I'll hand it over to Samir for quick status, then Priya will walk through the benchmark results and the upgrade plan.
00:12 Samir Patel: Yeah thanks Jordan. Quick update from our side, we got the VPC peering partially in place, the route tables are set but we've got an oddity with one of the NAT gateways where egress is blocking some of the health checks, so the Redwood pods aren't getting outbound.
00:29 Dana Ortiz: yeah that's right; we saw the tunnel flaps for a bit, had to reattach the route; looks like the source/dest check was still on one instance, my bad.
00:37 Priya Kapoor: OK that explains the intermittent failures we were seeing in the tail latencies. When nodes can't reach the registry we saw a restart loop and the KV cache warmup hadn't completed. FYI we log the warmups as K V cache in some of the older telemetry so there's a mismatch in the dashboards.
00:55 Emma Shaw: small question, when you say restart loop, is that during heavy traffic or during startup?
01:02 Priya Kapoor: Mostly startup during the initial rolling update to 1.2, but under heavy traffic we saw a single-digit percent increase in p99 when the cache misses spiked.
01:12 Jordan Lee: Right — and to be clear, the runtime 1.2 includes a fix for the attention kernel selection that should reduce those p99 spikes; we tested it in our lab.
01:21 Samir Patel: Any breaking changes we should be careful about?
01:25 Jordan Lee: There is a config flag name change for the batcher and the telemetry keys — it's harmless but you'll need to update the manifest. I'll send the patched manifest after the call.
01:34 Luca Romano: On the security side, we had one ask — can Redwood confirm that KMS keys are customer-managed and whether key rotation is supported via HSM? Also need to know what audit logs look like and retention.
01:44 Jordan Lee: Yes — for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. Rotation policy is supported, but the pilot is still on the standard rotation cadence; for HSM-backed keys we can bring the details, I'll get Marcus to share the vendor integration doc.
01:57 Marcus Nguyen: I'll drop the HSM integration doc and a snippet of the audit log format. Note that logs currently include per-request metadata but we can redact token content fields per your compliance needs.
02:07 Dana Ortiz: Great. Back to networking — Samir, can you paste the peering owner ID and CIDR ranges in the ticket?
02:12 Samir Patel: Yep will do after this call. I put a note in the ticket about the NAT issue.
02:18 Priya Kapoor: Alright, I'll go through the benchmark spreadsheet. We ran three scenarios: baseline hosted (for parity), initial private pilot (v1.1 runtime), and the new 1.2 build. The CSV is uploaded to the shared drive but I'll summarize — baseline p50 around 42ms, p95 around 120ms in our region; private v1.1 p50 at 65ms p95 ~210ms and p99 tails up to 620ms in the worst windows. The 1.2 build cut p99 tail by ~25% in lab but pilot hasn't had the upgrade everywhere so results are mixed.
02:55 Emma Shaw: Does the workload include multi-turn chat or just single-shot generation?
03:01 Priya Kapoor: Both. We included a multi-turn conversation workload with a lot of KV cache reuse and a single-shot prompt set for worst-case long-context generation. The multi-turn where prefix caching helped showed much better latency. The long-context single-shot is where we still see the p99 spikes if cache didn't populate.
03:17 Jordan Lee: Quick note, we also found that turning on the aggressive prefix caching option helps but it increases memory slightly; for your pilot nodes with 80GB RAM that's fine but if you scale down to 40GB you'll want to keep moderate caching.
03:30 Dana Ortiz: We're on 96GB nodes for this pilot so memory isn't immediate concern, more worried about the egress and firewall rules.
03:38 Jordan Lee: Understood. About the egress — Priya, what were the specific endpoints the runtime needs to reach during startup? I can paste the list.
03:45 Priya Kapoor: It's mainly our image registry, metrics endpoint (collect.redwood.ai), and the config service for rolling updates. The IPs are in the manifest but they resolved as hostnames; we can provide FQDNs too.
03:58 Samir Patel: We'll need FQDNs so security can allow via proxy rules.
04:03 Priya Kapoor: I'll add them to the ticket, thanks.
04:08 Luca Romano: On audit logs — how long do you retain them and can we increase retention for SOC2 evidence?
04:14 Marcus Nguyen: Default is 90 days in the pilot; for enterprise plans we can arrange custom retention or ship to your SIEM. I'll include retention options in the doc.
04:23 Jordan Lee: Cool. Next, upgrade plan: we propose a rolling upgrade, canary on 10% of nodes for 24 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99 and then accelerate if stable. Any objections?
04:36 Dana Ortiz: Sounds good, but ensure we can roll back quickly; last time the rollback script didn't decommission the newer cache properly.
04:44 Priya Kapoor: We'll include a rollback step that flushes the KV cache sequence and pins the old runtime. Should be safe. Also note config flag change — we'll include a one-line migration note.
04:58 Samir Patel: Timeline wise we want to finish the upgrade by next Wednesday, so if you can send the manifest and we run the canary on Monday that works for us.
05:08 Jordan Lee: I'll send the manifest today.
05:11 Emma Shaw: On benchmarks, can you also share the request traces around the p99 spikes? We want to see actual call patterns.
05:18 Priya Kapoor: Yes — we have sampled traces and I'll anonymize them and upload the trace ids with the CSV. Note some traces have mis-labeled service names in our internal telemetry, so if a name looks off that's likely a transcription or service rename.
05:33 Jordan Lee: Any other blockers?
05:35 Samir Patel: Just the NAT/peering update and the CIDRs. Once those are in we can run the broader 1.2 canary.
05:42 Luca Romano: Security side is ok as long as HSM details are confirmed and audit retention is agreed. I'll review the vendor doc.
05:50 Marcus Nguyen: I'll follow up with HSM doc and audit retention options by EOD.
05:57 Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap and next steps — I'll send the patched manifest (runtime 1.2 changes) and a short upgrade checklist. Priya will run the 1k-request latency suite and CSV, and Samir will add peering details to the ticket. Marcus will share HSM integration docs and audit options.
06:15 Emma Shaw: Can you also send estimated cost delta for running 1.2 with aggressive caching? We just want rough numbers for planning.
06:22 Jordan Lee: Yes I'll include rough delta (expected +6-8% memory footprint cost, which maps to about +3-5% infra spend based on your node sizes).
06:31 Samir Patel: I'll coordinate with finance.
06:33 Jordan Lee: Anything else?
06:35 Dana Ortiz: Nope all good from SRE.
06:37 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and reconvene next week same time.

Action Items (spoken in call):
- Jordan Lee to send updated deployment manifest and upgrade checklist (due 2027-11-29)
- Priya Kapoor to run 1k-request latency benchmark and upload results + traces (due 2027-11-30)
- Samir Patel to provide CIDR ranges, peering owner IDs and note NAT gateway fix (due 2027-11-28)
- Marcus Nguyen to share HSM integration doc and audit retention options (due 2027-11-25 EOD)

Links referenced: (in chat) shared drive: drive.company/tds-redwood/pilot-benchmarks.csv, ticket: #TD-4382, HSM doc placeholder: redwood-internal/docs/hsm-integration.pdf

End of transcript.
